controls.evidence_requirement: Asset inventory, classification policy.

controls.title: Identity and Access Management
controls.description: Governs provisioning, authentication, and authorization of access to systems and data based on least privilege.
controls.test_criteria: Review access provisioning records and periodic access review evidence.
controls.evidence_requirement: Access control policy, access review logs.

controls.title: Information System and Information Processing Facilities Protection
controls.description: Requires secure configuration and protection of information systems and the facilities that host them.
controls.test_criteria: Review system hardening configuration and facility protection controls.
controls.evidence_requirement: Hardening standards, configuration audit reports.

controls.title: Email Protection
controls.description: Requires security controls to protect email systems against phishing, spoofing, and malware.
controls.test_criteria: Review email security gateway and anti-spoofing (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) configuration.
controls.evidence_requirement: Email security configuration, DMARC/SPF/DKIM records.

controls.title: Networks Security Management
controls.description: Requires network segmentation, firewalls, and secure configuration of network infrastructure.
controls.test_criteria: Review network architecture and firewall rule-base review records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Network diagrams, firewall rule reviews.

controls.title: Mobile Devices Security
controls.description: Requires security controls for mobile devices accessing organizational networks and data.
controls.test_criteria: Review MDM policy enforcement for mobile devices.
controls.evidence_requirement: MDM policy and compliance reports.

controls.title: Data and Information Protection
controls.description: Requires classification, handling, and protection controls for data throughout its lifecycle.
controls.test_criteria: Review data classification application and protection controls matching classification level.
controls.evidence_requirement: Data classification policy, data protection control evidence.

controls.title: Cryptography
controls.description: Specifies approved cryptographic standards and key management practices for protecting data confidentiality and integrity.
controls.test_criteria: Review cryptographic configuration and key management procedures against approved standards.
controls.evidence_requirement: Cryptographic standards, key management procedures.

controls.title: Backup and Recovery Management
controls.description: Requires regular backups and tested recovery procedures for critical systems and data.
controls.test_criteria: Review backup schedules and restoration test results.
controls.evidence_requirement: Backup policy, backup logs, restoration test reports.

controls.title: Vulnerability Management
controls.description: Requires regular vulnerability scanning and timely remediation of identified weaknesses.
controls.test_criteria: Review vulnerability scan reports and remediation timelines.
controls.evidence_requirement: Vulnerability scan reports, remediation tracker.

controls.title: Penetration Testing
controls.description: Requires periodic penetration testing of critical systems to validate the effectiveness of security controls.
controls.test_criteria: Review penetration test scope, findings, and remediation evidence.
controls.evidence_requirement: Penetration test reports, remediation/retest evidence.

controls.title: Cybersecurity Event Logs and Monitoring Management
controls.description: Requires centralized logging and continuous monitoring to detect security events and anomalies.
controls.test_criteria: Review logging configuration and sample monitoring/alert handling records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Logging standards, SIEM configuration, alert logs.

controls.title: Cybersecurity Incident and Threat Management
controls.description: Requires processes to detect, respond to, and recover from cybersecurity incidents and threats, including reporting to the NCA where required.
controls.test_criteria: Review incident response plan and sample incident records including regulatory reporting timeliness.
controls.evidence_requirement: Incident response plan, incident log, NCA reporting records.

controls.title: Physical Security
controls.description: Requires physical access controls and environmental protections for facilities housing information systems.
controls.test_criteria: Review physical access logs and facility security inspection records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Physical access logs, facility security assessment.

controls.title: Cybersecurity Resilience (Business Continuity)
controls.description: Requires cybersecurity resilience considerations be embedded into business continuity management, ensuring critical services remain available during cyber disruptions.
controls.test_criteria: Review BCM plans for cybersecurity-specific resilience scenarios and test results.
controls.evidence_requirement: Business continuity plan, cyber resilience test/exercise reports.

controls.title: Third-Party Cybersecurity
controls.description: Requires cybersecurity requirements and due diligence for third parties with access to organizational systems or data.
controls.test_criteria: Review third-party risk assessments and contractual cybersecurity requirements.
controls.evidence_requirement: Vendor risk assessments, contracts with security clauses.

controls.title: Cloud Computing and Hosting Cybersecurity
controls.description: Requires cybersecurity controls and due diligence for data and workloads hosted with cloud service providers, including data residency considerations.
controls.test_criteria: Review cloud provider security assessments and data residency/compliance verification.
controls.evidence_requirement: Cloud provider due-diligence records, cloud security configuration evidence.

controls.title: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) Cybersecurity
controls.description: Requires cybersecurity controls tailored to industrial control systems/OT environments, addressing their unique availability and safety requirements.
controls.test_criteria: Review ICS/OT network segmentation and ICS-specific security control implementation.
controls.evidence_requirement: ICS network architecture, ICS security control documentation.

name: PHIPA
description: Ontario's Personal Health Information Protection Act, 2004 governs the collection, use, and disclosure of personal health information by health information custodians in Ontario, Canada; it is enforced by the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario (IPC).
notes: PHIPA is a provincial (Ontario) statute, not federal Canadian law (contrast with PIPEDA). Controls below reflect the Act's substantive Parts (I-VI.1) plus its regulation (O. Reg. 329/04) at a top-level, non-exhaustive granularity appropriate for a control library.

controls.title: Health Information Custodian Determination
controls.description: Identify whether the organization/individual is a health information custodian (HIC) as defined in s.3, and classify the type of custodian (hospital, physician, pharmacy, etc.) to determine applicable obligations.
controls.test_criteria: Documented custodian determination and role mapping reviewed against the s.3 statutory definitions.
controls.evidence_requirement: Custodian classification memo; org chart mapping roles to HIC categories.

controls.title: Information Practices Statement
controls.description: HICs must maintain a publicly available written statement of information practices describing how PHI is handled, the contact person for privacy inquiries, and the complaint process.
controls.test_criteria: Review published privacy policy/statement for completeness and public accessibility.
controls.evidence_requirement: Published privacy statement; website/intake materials; privacy officer contact information.

controls.title: Designation of Contact Person / Privacy Officer
controls.description: An HIC may designate an agent as a contact person responsible for PHIPA compliance, facilitating access requests and handling complaints.
controls.test_criteria: Verify formal designation and a job description covering PHIPA-specific duties.
controls.evidence_requirement: Appointment letter; privacy officer role description.

controls.title: Consent Requirements
controls.description: PHI may only be collected, used, or disclosed with the knowledgeable consent of the individual (express or implied) unless collection, use, or disclosure without consent is permitted or required by law.
controls.test_criteria: Sample records to verify consent was captured or a lawful exception was documented.
controls.evidence_requirement: Consent forms; EHR consent flags; exception justification logs.

controls.title: Elements of Valid Consent
controls.description: Consent must relate to the information in question, be knowledgeable, be given voluntarily, and not be obtained through fraud or misrepresentation.
controls.test_criteria: Review the consent capture workflow/scripts for the presence of all required elements.
controls.evidence_requirement: Consent capture UI or script; front-line staff training materials.

controls.title: Withdrawal of Consent / Lock-box
controls.description: Individuals may withdraw or withhold consent to future collection, use, or disclosure of their PHI (subject to exceptions), and HICs must accommodate such instructions, commonly called a 'lock-box'.
controls.test_criteria: Test the system's ability to flag and restrict PHI per a patient's lock-box instruction.
controls.evidence_requirement: System configuration for consent directives; audit of honored lock-box requests.

controls.title: Limiting Collection, Use and Disclosure
controls.description: PHI collection, use, and disclosure must be limited to what is reasonably necessary for the identified purpose, with specific permitted disclosure grounds (e.g., health care, public health, law enforcement).
controls.test_criteria: Review data flows/interfaces against necessity criteria and permitted statutory grounds.
controls.evidence_requirement: Data flow diagrams; disclosure logs mapped to permitted grounds.

controls.title: Reasonable Safeguards
controls.description: HICs must implement reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect PHI against theft, loss, and unauthorized use, disclosure, copying, modification, or disposal.
controls.test_criteria: Review the safeguards inventory (access controls, encryption, physical security) against the organization's risk assessment.
controls.evidence_requirement: Safeguards policy; risk assessment; access control logs; encryption configuration evidence.

controls.title: Secure Retention, Transfer and Disposal
controls.description: PHI must be retained, transferred, and disposed of securely in accordance with O. Reg. 329/04 requirements, including approved secure destruction methods.
controls.test_criteria: Review the retention schedule and destruction certificates/logs for secure disposal practices.
controls.evidence_requirement: Retention schedule; certificates of destruction; secure disposal vendor contracts.

controls.title: Right of Access
controls.description: Individuals have a right to access their own record of PHI held by an HIC, subject to limited exceptions, within prescribed response timelines (generally 30 days).
controls.test_criteria: Review the access request log for timeliness and completeness of responses.
controls.evidence_requirement: Access request tracking log; sample response letters.

controls.title: Right of Correction
controls.description: Individuals may request correction of inaccurate or incomplete PHI; the HIC must correct the record or annotate it with a statement of disagreement if correction is refused.
controls.test_criteria: Review the correction request handling process and sample outcomes.
controls.evidence_requirement: Correction request log; amended records; statements of disagreement on file.

controls.title: Complaints and IPC Review
controls.description: HICs must maintain a process for receiving and responding to privacy complaints, and must cooperate with Information and Privacy Commissioner reviews, investigations, and orders.
controls.test_criteria: Review the complaint log and evidence of cooperation with any IPC proceedings.
controls.evidence_requirement: Complaint register; IPC correspondence; order compliance records.

controls.title: Breach Notification
controls.description: HICs must notify affected individuals at the first reasonable opportunity if PHI is stolen, lost, or used/disclosed without authority, and must notify the IPC in prescribed circumstances, including mandatory reporting thresholds under O. Reg. 329/04 s.6.3.
controls.test_criteria: Review the breach log for notification timeliness to individuals and the IPC against regulated thresholds.
controls.evidence_requirement: Breach register; notification letters; IPC breach reports.

controls.title: Electronic Health Record (EHR) Provisions
controls.description: Custodians contributing to or using a consolidated electronic health record are subject to additional obligations under Part V.1, including Health Information Network Provider (HINP) agreements and enhanced logging/auditing.
controls.test_criteria: Review HINP agreements and EHR access audit logs for compliance with Part V.1 requirements.
controls.evidence_requirement: HINP agreement; EHR audit trail reports.

controls.title: Agent Management
controls.description: HICs remain responsible for PHI handled by their agents, including service providers, and must have agreements restricting agents' collection, use, and disclosure to purposes authorized by the custodian.
controls.test_criteria: Review agent and service-provider agreements for PHIPA-compliant clauses.
controls.evidence_requirement: Signed agent agreements; data processing addenda; agent training records.

controls.title: Research Disclosures
controls.description: Disclosure of PHI for research purposes without consent requires research ethics board (REB) approval and a data-sharing agreement meeting prescribed requirements.
controls.test_criteria: Review REB approvals and research data-sharing agreements supporting PHI disclosures.
controls.evidence_requirement: REB approval letters; research data-sharing agreements.

controls.title: De-Identification and Aggregation
controls.description: Where practicable, HICs should use de-identified or aggregate information in place of identifiable PHI when identifiable data is not necessary for the stated purpose.
controls.test_criteria: Review the de-identification methodology and documented use cases where identifiable data was avoided.
controls.evidence_requirement: De-identification standard/methodology; data-use justification records.

controls.title: Workforce Privacy Training
controls.description: Agents and staff with access to PHI must receive privacy and security training appropriate to their role and level of access.
controls.test_criteria: Review training completion records and curriculum content for role-appropriateness.
controls.evidence_requirement: Training curriculum; completion logs/certificates.

name: Cyber Essentials V3.2
description: The UK NCSC's Cyber Essentials scheme is a government-backed, industry-supported certification defining a baseline of five technical control themes to protect organizations against common internet-based cyber attacks; it is administered by IASME on behalf of the NCSC.
notes: The scheme's question set is updated periodically (e.g., v3.1 effective Jan 2023, later revisions through 2024-2025); verify the exact in-force version and any version-specific wording changes against the current IASME/NCSC published question set before citing externally. The 5 control themes (firewalls, secure configuration, security update management, user access control, malware protection) are stable across recent versions; this list breaks them into assessable sub-requirements.

controls.title: Scope and Boundary Definition
controls.description: The organization must define the whole-organization scope, or a sub-set boundary with documented segregation, covering all in-scope end-user devices, servers, network devices, and cloud services (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS) used to conduct business.
controls.test_criteria: Review the scope statement and network diagram against the certification body's assessment boundary rules.
controls.evidence_requirement: Scope declaration document; network architecture diagram; cloud service inventory.

controls.title: Boundary Firewalls
controls.description: All internet-connected devices must be protected by a correctly configured firewall, or equivalent network device, at the network boundary.
controls.test_criteria: Verify firewall deployment and rule review for default-deny inbound posture with documented business-justified exceptions.
controls.evidence_requirement: Firewall configuration export; firewall rule review log.

controls.title: Firewall Administrative Access
controls.description: Default administrative passwords on firewalls must be changed, and firewall administrative interfaces must not be accessible from the internet unless protected by multi-factor authentication.
controls.test_criteria: Verify administrative credential rotation and remote management access controls/MFA.
controls.evidence_requirement: Credential rotation record; firewall administrative access configuration screenshot.

controls.title: Software Firewalls on Mobile Devices
controls.description: Devices used outside a protected network boundary (e.g., laptops) must run a correctly configured host-based (software) firewall.
controls.test_criteria: Sample endpoint configurations to confirm the host firewall is enabled and correctly configured.
controls.evidence_requirement: Endpoint configuration management report/screenshot.

controls.title: Removal of Unnecessary Software and Accounts
controls.description: Unnecessary user accounts, default/guest accounts, and unused software or services must be removed or disabled on all in-scope devices.
controls.test_criteria: Review the device build standard and sample device configuration against the inventory of installed software/accounts.
controls.evidence_requirement: Device build/hardening standard; software inventory report.

controls.title: Autorun/Autoplay and Default Settings
controls.description: Autorun/autoplay features must be disabled, and any pre-installed or default applications that are not needed must be removed or disabled.
controls.test_criteria: Sample device checks to confirm autorun/autoplay is disabled.
controls.evidence_requirement: Group Policy/MDM configuration export.

controls.title: Authentication Before Access
controls.description: All devices and software must require authentication, such as a unique user account and password or biometric, before granting access.
controls.test_criteria: Verify the device lock/authentication screen configuration across sampled devices.
controls.evidence_requirement: Device policy configuration screenshot.

controls.title: User Account Creation and Approval
controls.description: A formal process must govern user account creation, approval, and removal, ensuring accounts are only created for identified, approved individuals.
controls.test_criteria: Review the joiner/mover/leaver process and sample account creation records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Access provisioning procedure; sample approval tickets.

controls.title: Authentication Controls (Passwords/MFA)
controls.description: Organizations must enforce a password policy (minimum length, deny common passwords, lockout/throttling) and/or MFA, with MFA mandatory for cloud services, administrative accounts, and remote access.
controls.test_criteria: Review authentication policy configuration and MFA enrollment for cloud and administrative accounts.
controls.evidence_requirement: Password policy configuration; MFA enrollment report.

controls.title: Administrative Account Management
controls.description: Administrative privileges must be assigned only to approved, necessary users; admin accounts must not be used for day-to-day tasks such as email or browsing; and the number of admins must be kept to a minimum and regularly reviewed.
controls.test_criteria: Review the privileged account inventory and separation-of-duties evidence.
controls.evidence_requirement: Privileged access register; periodic access review records.

controls.title: Account Removal and Access Review
controls.description: User accounts must be removed or disabled promptly when no longer required, and access rights must be reviewed on a regular basis.
controls.test_criteria: Review leaver process timeliness and periodic access review logs.
controls.evidence_requirement: Leaver tickets with timestamps; access review reports.

controls.title: Malware Protection - Anti-Malware Software
controls.description: All devices must run anti-malware software that is kept up to date, configured to scan files on access/download, and configured to prevent connections to known malicious websites.
controls.test_criteria: Verify anti-malware deployment, update status, and configuration across sampled devices.
controls.evidence_requirement: Endpoint protection console report; update/version logs.

controls.title: Application Allow Listing / Sandboxing
controls.description: Where anti-malware software is not used on a device, the organization must use application allow listing or run untrusted applications in an isolated sandbox.
controls.test_criteria: Verify configuration of application allow-listing or sandboxing controls on applicable devices.
controls.evidence_requirement: Application control policy export; approved application list.

controls.title: Security Update (Patch) Management
controls.description: All software, including operating systems, firmware, and applications, must be licensed and supported, removed when it reaches end of support, and have security updates for critical/high-severity vulnerabilities applied within 14 days of release.
controls.test_criteria: Review patch management reports for compliance with the 14-day critical/high patching window and review the unsupported-software inventory.
controls.evidence_requirement: Patch compliance report; vulnerability scan results; software support-status inventory.

name: CMMC 2.13 Level 3
description: The US Department of Defense's Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 3 (Expert) requires defense contractors handling Controlled Unclassified Information tied to critical programs or high-value assets to implement all NIST SP 800-171 controls (Level 2) plus 24 enhanced requirements drawn from NIST SP 800-172, verified through a government-led (DIBCAC) assessment.
notes: The official DoD program designation is 'CMMC 2.0,' codified in the DoD final rule at 32 CFR Part 170 (published October 15, 2024; effective December 16, 2024), with the companion DFARS acquisition rule (48 CFR 252.204-7021) following to begin contract phase-in. 'CMMC 2.13' as given in this task does not correspond to an official DoD regulatory version number; it appears in third-party compliance tooling (e.g., Apptega, Check Point, Trend Micro release notes) as a documentation/model-guide version label for the CMMC Level 1/2/3 Assessment Guides released in the 2024-2025 timeframe, built on the same 32 CFR Part 170 final rule. This entry describes current CMMC 2.0 Level 3 substantive requirements; treat the '2.13' label as a third-party tooling/document version rather than a distinct regulatory version, and verify against the live DoD CMMC program page before citing it externally. Level 3 also references NIST SP 800-172 (Feb 2021 edition); a Revision 3 of SP 800-172 may be in progress but has not been confirmed as adopted by CMMC.

controls.title: Access Control
controls.description: Limit system access to authorized users, processes, and devices, and to the types of transactions and functions permitted; Level 3 adds enhanced requirements for privileged account and session controls against Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs), per NIST SP 800-172.
controls.test_criteria: Review access control policy, account inventory, and the implementation of enhanced (800-172) privileged access controls.
controls.evidence_requirement: Access control policy; account review logs; privileged access monitoring reports.

controls.title: Awareness and Training
controls.description: Ensure personnel are adequately trained to carry out their assigned security-related duties and are aware of security risks, including APT-specific threat awareness required at Level 3.
controls.test_criteria: Review the training curriculum and completion records for inclusion of APT-focused content.
controls.evidence_requirement: Training records; APT awareness training materials.

controls.title: Audit and Accountability
controls.description: Create, protect, and retain system audit records enabling monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting of unlawful or unauthorized activity; Level 3 requires enhanced log collection and correlation to support advanced threat detection.
controls.test_criteria: Review audit log configuration, retention, and the organization's correlation/SIEM capability.
controls.evidence_requirement: Audit log policy; SIEM configuration; sample audit reports.

controls.title: Security Assessment
controls.description: Periodically assess security controls, develop and update a Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M), and monitor control effectiveness; Level 3 requires a DIBCAC-led government assessment approximately every three years plus continuous monitoring posture.
controls.test_criteria: Review self-assessment/POA&M records and readiness artifacts for a DIBCAC-led assessment.
controls.evidence_requirement: System Security Plan (SSP); POA&M; prior assessment results.

controls.title: Configuration Management
controls.description: Establish and maintain baseline configurations and inventories, and control changes to systems throughout their lifecycle; Level 3 adds enhanced configuration integrity verification controls from NIST SP 800-172.
controls.test_criteria: Review configuration baselines, change control records, and integrity monitoring tooling.
controls.evidence_requirement: Baseline configuration documents; change control tickets; configuration integrity monitoring logs.

controls.title: Identification and Authentication
controls.description: Identify system users, processes, and devices, and authenticate their identities before granting access; Level 3 adds enhanced requirements for phishing-resistant MFA and identity assurance against APTs.
controls.test_criteria: Review authentication mechanisms including MFA strength and identity-proofing procedures.
controls.evidence_requirement: Authentication system configuration; MFA deployment report.

controls.title: Incident Response
controls.description: Establish an operational incident-handling capability including preparation, detection, analysis, containment, recovery, and reporting; Level 3 requires enhanced response capability for sophisticated, advanced threats.
controls.test_criteria: Review the incident response plan, tabletop exercise records, and procedures for reporting to DoD (DIBNet).
controls.evidence_requirement: Incident response plan; exercise after-action reports; incident reports filed.

controls.title: Maintenance
controls.description: Perform periodic and timely maintenance on systems, and provide effective controls on the tools, techniques, mechanisms, and personnel used to conduct maintenance.
controls.test_criteria: Review maintenance logs and controls over maintenance personnel and tools, including remote maintenance.
controls.evidence_requirement: Maintenance records; remote maintenance session logs.

controls.title: Media Protection
controls.description: Protect system media, both paper and digital, containing CUI, including marking, access restriction, transport controls, and sanitization/destruction before disposal or reuse.
controls.test_criteria: Review media handling procedures and sanitization/destruction records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Media protection policy; sanitization certificates.

controls.title: Personnel Security
controls.description: Screen individuals before authorizing access to systems containing CUI, and ensure CUI protection during and after personnel actions such as transfer or termination.
controls.test_criteria: Review personnel screening and offboarding records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Screening/background check records; termination checklists.

controls.title: Physical Protection
controls.description: Limit physical access to systems, equipment, and operating environments to authorized individuals, and protect and monitor the physical facility and support infrastructure.
controls.test_criteria: Review physical access control logs and visitor management records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Badge access logs; visitor logs; facility security plan.

controls.title: Risk Assessment
controls.description: Periodically assess the risk to operations, assets, and individuals arising from the operation of systems and processing of CUI; Level 3 adds enhanced threat-hunting and advanced risk analysis capability.
controls.test_criteria: Review risk assessment reports and artifacts documenting a threat hunting program.
controls.evidence_requirement: Risk assessment report; threat hunting program documentation.

controls.title: System and Communications Protection
controls.description: Monitor, control, and protect communications at external and key internal system boundaries; Level 3 adds enhanced requirements such as network segmentation and isolation against advanced adversaries.
controls.test_criteria: Review network architecture, boundary protection devices, and segmentation testing evidence.
controls.evidence_requirement: Network diagrams; boundary protection device configurations; segmentation test results.

controls.title: System and Information Integrity
controls.description: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner; provide protection from malicious code; monitor system security alerts; Level 3 adds enhanced requirements for advanced malware/APT detection, including threat intelligence integration.
controls.test_criteria: Review vulnerability management, malware protection, and advanced threat detection capability.
controls.evidence_requirement: Vulnerability scan reports; patch records; threat intelligence feed integration evidence.

name: EU AI Act
description: The European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is a risk-tiered legal framework governing the development, deployment, and use of AI systems in the EU, enforced by the European AI Office and national market surveillance authorities, with obligations phased in through 2027.
notes: Entered into force August 1, 2024. Prohibited-practice provisions applied from February 2, 2025; general-purpose AI (GPAI) model obligations from August 2, 2025; most high-risk system obligations apply from August 2, 2026 (Annex III use cases) or August 2, 2027 (Annex I regulated products). Controls below reflect top-level Titles/Articles.

controls.title: Prohibited AI Practices
controls.description: Certain AI practices are banned outright, including subliminal or manipulative techniques causing harm, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement (with narrow exceptions), and emotion inference in workplaces/education (with exceptions).
controls.test_criteria: Review the AI use-case inventory against the Article 5 prohibited-practice criteria.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI use-case register; legal review memo confirming no prohibited practices.

controls.title: Risk Classification / AI System Inventory
controls.description: Organizations must classify each AI system by risk tier (unacceptable, high-risk, limited-risk/transparency, minimal risk) based on Annex III use cases and the system's intended purpose.
controls.test_criteria: Review the classification methodology and the documented risk tier assigned to each AI system.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI system risk classification register; classification decision records.

controls.title: Risk Management System (High-Risk)
controls.description: Providers of high-risk AI systems must establish, implement, document, and maintain a continuous risk management system across the system's entire lifecycle.
controls.test_criteria: Review risk management process documentation and evidence of iterative risk identification and mitigation.
controls.evidence_requirement: Risk management system documentation; risk register; mitigation records.

controls.title: Data and Data Governance
controls.description: Training, validation, and testing datasets for high-risk AI systems must meet quality criteria such as relevance, representativeness, error examination, and bias mitigation, supported by appropriate data governance practices.
controls.test_criteria: Review dataset governance documentation and bias/quality testing results.
controls.evidence_requirement: Data governance policy; dataset quality/bias test reports.

controls.title: Technical Documentation
controls.description: Providers must draw up technical documentation demonstrating compliance before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, in line with the content required by Annex IV.
controls.test_criteria: Review the technical documentation against the required Annex IV elements.
controls.evidence_requirement: Technical documentation file.

controls.title: Record-Keeping (Logging)
controls.description: High-risk AI systems must have logging capabilities that enable traceability of the system's operation appropriate to its intended purpose.
controls.test_criteria: Review logging configuration and sample logs for adequate traceability.
controls.evidence_requirement: System logs; logging architecture documentation.

controls.title: Transparency and Instructions for Use
controls.description: High-risk AI systems must be accompanied by instructions for use that enable deployers to interpret the system's output and use it appropriately.
controls.test_criteria: Review the instructions for use/documentation provided to deployers.
controls.evidence_requirement: User/deployer instructions; product documentation.

controls.title: Human Oversight
controls.description: High-risk AI systems must be designed to allow effective human oversight, including the ability for a human to intervene in, override, or stop the system.
controls.test_criteria: Review human oversight design features and tested override/stop mechanisms.
controls.evidence_requirement: Human oversight design documentation; test records of override functionality.

controls.title: Accuracy, Robustness, and Cybersecurity
controls.description: High-risk AI systems must achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and be resilient to errors, faults, and attempts at adversarial manipulation.
controls.test_criteria: Review accuracy/robustness test results and cybersecurity testing, including adversarial testing.
controls.evidence_requirement: Performance test reports; security/penetration test reports.

controls.title: Provider Conformity and Market Placement Obligations
controls.description: Providers of high-risk AI systems must implement a quality management system, retain documentation, undergo conformity assessment, affix CE marking, and register the system in the EU database before placing it on the market.
controls.test_criteria: Review QMS documentation, the conformity assessment certificate, and the EU database registration record.
controls.evidence_requirement: QMS documentation; conformity assessment report; EU database registration confirmation.

controls.title: Deployer Obligations
controls.description: Deployers of high-risk AI systems must use the systems in accordance with instructions, assign human oversight to competent personnel, and monitor operation of the system.
controls.test_criteria: Review deployer operating procedures and human oversight assignment records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Deployer usage procedures; oversight assignment records.

controls.title: Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment
controls.description: Certain deployers, such as public bodies and specific private entities, must conduct a Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment before deploying a high-risk AI system.
controls.test_criteria: Review the FRIA methodology and completed assessments for applicable deployments.
controls.evidence_requirement: FRIA reports; stakeholder consultation records.

controls.title: Transparency Obligations for Certain AI Systems
controls.description: Providers and deployers must disclose AI interaction to users (e.g., chatbots), label AI-generated or manipulated content (e.g., deepfakes), and disclose the use of emotion recognition or biometric categorization systems to affected individuals.
controls.test_criteria: Review the disclosure mechanisms and content-labeling implementation.
controls.evidence_requirement: Disclosure notices/UI screenshots; content watermarking/labeling evidence.

controls.title: GPAI Model Obligations
controls.description: Providers of general-purpose AI models must maintain technical documentation, provide information to downstream providers, implement a copyright-compliance policy, and publish a sufficiently detailed summary of training content.
controls.test_criteria: Review GPAI technical documentation, the downstream information package, and the published training-data summary.
controls.evidence_requirement: GPAI model documentation; copyright compliance policy; training data summary publication.

controls.title: Systemic Risk GPAI Obligations
controls.description: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, as determined by compute and other thresholds, must perform model evaluation, adversarial testing, incident tracking/reporting, and ensure adequate cybersecurity protection.
controls.test_criteria: Review systemic-risk model evaluation and incident tracking records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Model evaluation reports; adversarial/red-team testing results; incident log.

controls.title: Quality Management System
controls.description: Providers of high-risk AI systems must implement a documented quality management system covering regulatory compliance strategy, design control, data management, and post-market monitoring.
controls.test_criteria: Review the QMS scope and document control records.
controls.evidence_requirement: QMS manual; internal audit records.

controls.title: Post-Market Monitoring
controls.description: Providers must establish and document a post-market monitoring system to actively and systematically collect and review experience from the use of high-risk AI systems.
controls.test_criteria: Review the post-market monitoring plan and collected field performance/incident data.
controls.evidence_requirement: Post-market monitoring plan; field performance reports.

controls.title: Serious Incident Reporting
controls.description: Providers must report serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems to the relevant market surveillance authorities within prescribed timeframes.
controls.test_criteria: Review the incident reporting procedure and sample reports filed with authorities.
controls.evidence_requirement: Incident reporting procedure; submitted incident reports.

controls.title: AI Literacy
controls.description: Providers and deployers must ensure that staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems have a sufficient level of AI literacy, considering their technical knowledge and the context of use.
controls.test_criteria: Review the AI literacy training program and completion records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Training curriculum; completion logs.

controls.title: Governance and Competent Authorities
controls.description: Organizations must identify and cooperate with the relevant national competent/market surveillance authority and, for GPAI models, the EU AI Office, and must maintain a designated compliance contact.
controls.test_criteria: Review the documented regulatory contact mapping and records of cooperation with authority requests.
controls.evidence_requirement: Regulatory contact register; correspondence with authorities.

name: ISO 27701:2025
description: ISO/IEC 27701:2025 is the international standard for a Privacy Information Management System (PIMS), published October 14, 2025 as a standalone second edition that can be implemented independently of (though still aligned with) ISO/IEC 27001/27002, providing requirements and guidance for PII controllers and processors.
notes: Confirmed via current research: ISO/IEC 27701:2025 is a real, newly published second edition (dated mid-October 2025, sources vary between the 10th and 14th), superseding the 2019 edition, which was structured strictly as an extension to ISO/IEC 27001. The major structural change in the 2025 edition is that it can stand alone without requiring certification to ISO/IEC 27001, while remaining aligned with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and 27002:2022. Because the standard is very newly published, detailed public clause-by-clause breakdowns are still emerging; the control list below reflects the standard's known structure (general PIMS management-system requirements plus controller/processor-specific annex control themes carried over conceptually from the 2019 edition) and should be revalidated against the full published text as implementation guidance matures. Certification bodies report a transition period from the 2019 edition of roughly 24-36 months.

controls.title: PIMS Context and Scope
controls.description: The organization must determine the scope of the Privacy Information Management System, considering its role(s) as PII controller and/or processor and applicable privacy legislation.
controls.test_criteria: Review the PIMS scope statement and role determination for completeness.
controls.evidence_requirement: PIMS scope document; applicability statement.

controls.title: Leadership and Privacy Policy
controls.description: Top management must establish a privacy policy and ensure privacy objectives are integrated into organizational processes, with clearly assigned roles and responsibilities.
controls.test_criteria: Review privacy policy approval and the assignment of PIMS roles.
controls.evidence_requirement: Approved privacy policy; roles and responsibilities documentation.

controls.title: Privacy Risk Assessment and Treatment
controls.description: The organization must conduct a PII-specific risk assessment, including risk to PII principals and not only to the organization, and implement a corresponding risk treatment plan.
controls.test_criteria: Review the privacy risk assessment methodology and resulting risk treatment decisions.
controls.evidence_requirement: Privacy risk register; risk treatment plan.

controls.title: Resources, Competence and Awareness
controls.description: The organization must ensure adequate resources, competence, and awareness among personnel involved in PIMS operation, including privacy-specific training.
controls.test_criteria: Review training records and resource allocation for the privacy function.
controls.evidence_requirement: Training completion records; privacy team resourcing plan.

controls.title: Operational Planning and Control
controls.description: The organization must plan, implement, and control the processes needed to meet PIMS requirements, including management of outsourced processes affecting PII.
controls.test_criteria: Review operational procedures and outsourcing control records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Operating procedures; vendor management records.

controls.title: Performance Evaluation
controls.description: The organization must monitor, measure, analyze, and evaluate PIMS performance, including internal audits and management review.
controls.test_criteria: Review internal audit reports and management review minutes.
controls.evidence_requirement: Internal audit reports; management review records.

controls.title: Improvement
controls.description: The organization must address nonconformities and continually improve the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the PIMS.
controls.test_criteria: Review corrective action records and documented improvement initiatives.
controls.evidence_requirement: Nonconformity/CAPA log; improvement plan.

controls.title: Conditions for Collection and Processing (Controller)
controls.description: PII controllers must identify and document the lawful basis or purpose for collecting and processing PII, and determine when consent is the appropriate basis.
controls.test_criteria: Review purpose and lawful-basis documentation for each processing activity.
controls.evidence_requirement: Record of processing activities (RoPA); lawful basis determinations.

controls.title: Obligations to PII Principals
controls.description: Controllers must provide notice to PII principals, support rights of access, correction, and erasure, and provide mechanisms for complaints.
controls.test_criteria: Review the privacy notice and rights-fulfillment process evidence.
controls.evidence_requirement: Privacy notices; data subject request log.

controls.title: Privacy by Design and by Default
controls.description: Controllers must implement privacy-by-design and by-default principles in system and process design, including data minimization.
controls.test_criteria: Review the privacy-by-design checklist and its integration into the project lifecycle (e.g., DPIA gating).
controls.evidence_requirement: Privacy-by-design checklist; DPIA records for new projects.

controls.title: PII Sharing, Transfer, and Disclosure
controls.description: Controllers must identify the basis for transferring or sharing PII with third parties and jurisdictions and record such transfers, including cross-border transfer mechanisms.
controls.test_criteria: Review the transfer mapping and transfer mechanism documentation, such as standard contractual clauses.
controls.evidence_requirement: Data transfer register; transfer agreements/SCCs.

controls.title: Processor Contractual Agreements
controls.description: PII processors must process PII only on documented instructions from the controller, formalized through a contract or data processing agreement.
controls.test_criteria: Review processor contracts for required PIMS clauses.
controls.evidence_requirement: Data processing agreements; subcontractor flow-down clauses.

controls.title: Processor Assistance to Controller
controls.description: Processors must assist controllers in fulfilling data subject rights requests and breach notification obligations.
controls.test_criteria: Review processor SLAs/procedures describing assistance provided to controllers.
controls.evidence_requirement: SLA documentation; assistance request logs.

controls.title: Sub-processor Management
controls.description: Processors must obtain authorization before engaging sub-processors and ensure equivalent privacy obligations flow down to them.
controls.test_criteria: Review sub-processor authorization records and flow-down contract clauses.
controls.evidence_requirement: Sub-processor list; authorization approvals; flow-down contracts.

controls.title: PII Breach Management
controls.description: Controllers and processors must have documented procedures for identifying, assessing, and notifying PII breaches to relevant authorities and affected principals.
controls.test_criteria: Review the breach response procedure and sample breach handling records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Breach response plan; breach register.

controls.title: Retention, Minimization and Disposal
controls.description: Controllers must define and enforce retention periods for PII and ensure secure disposal or anonymization when the data is no longer needed.
controls.test_criteria: Review the retention schedule and disposal evidence against defined periods.
controls.evidence_requirement: Retention policy; disposal/destruction logs.

controls.title: Legal and Regulatory Applicability Mapping
controls.description: The organization must identify and document applicable privacy laws and regulations relevant to its PIMS scope and jurisdictions of operation.
controls.test_criteria: Review the applicable legislation register and its update cadence.
controls.evidence_requirement: Applicable legislation register; legal review sign-off.

controls.title: Joint Controller Arrangements
controls.description: Where PII is jointly controlled, responsibilities between joint controllers must be documented and made transparent to PII principals.
controls.test_criteria: Review joint controller agreements for the allocation of responsibilities.
controls.evidence_requirement: Joint controller agreement; transparency notice to principals.

name: DPDPA 2023 (Integrated 2025 Rules)
description: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 together with the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (notified November 13, 2025) form the operative data protection regime for digital personal data processing in India, enforced by the Data Protection Board of India under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).
notes: The DPDP Rules, 2025 were notified via gazette notification G.S.R. 846(E) dated November 13, 2025 (some media report November 14), operationalizing the 2023 Act. Compliance timelines are phased: secondary sources describe staggered commencement tranches, with some obligations reportedly subject to an 18-month-style phase-in (e.g., one compliance tracker cites the Rule 6 security-safeguards baseline as applicable from May 13, 2027). Sources disagree on specific dates for individual obligations; verify exact commencement dates for each Rule/section against the official gazette text before relying on them for a specific compliance deadline.

controls.title: Consent Notice Requirements
controls.description: Data Fiduciaries must provide a clear, itemized notice, independent of other information, at or before seeking consent, specifying the personal data to be collected and the purpose of processing in the content and format prescribed by the Rules.
controls.test_criteria: Review consent notice templates for the itemized content required under the Rules.
controls.evidence_requirement: Consent notice templates; consent capture UI screenshots.

controls.title: Consent Manager Framework
controls.description: Organizations enabling consent management must register as a Consent Manager with the Data Protection Board (if acting as one) or integrate with a registered Consent Manager platform enabling principals to give, manage, and withdraw consent.
controls.test_criteria: Review the Consent Manager registration status or the integration architecture with a registered Consent Manager.
controls.evidence_requirement: Consent Manager registration certificate; integration documentation.

controls.title: Significant Data Fiduciary Obligations
controls.description: Entities notified as Significant Data Fiduciaries must appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India, appoint an independent data auditor, and conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) and audits.
controls.test_criteria: Review SDF designation status, DPO/auditor appointment records, and DPIA reports.
controls.evidence_requirement: DPO appointment letter; independent audit report; DPIA documentation.

controls.title: Security Safeguards (Rule 6)
controls.description: Data Fiduciaries must implement reasonable security safeguards including encryption, access controls, monitoring/logging for unauthorized access, data backup for continuity, and retention of logs for at least one year.
controls.test_criteria: Review the technical safeguard implementation (encryption, access logs, backup) against the Rule 6 baseline.
controls.evidence_requirement: Encryption configuration evidence; access log retention records; backup policy/test results.

controls.title: Personal Data Breach Notification (Rule 7)
controls.description: Data Fiduciaries must notify the Data Protection Board and affected Data Principals of a personal data breach, with specified content, within Board-prescribed timelines, followed by a detailed report.
controls.test_criteria: Review the breach notification procedure and sample notifications sent to the Board and affected principals.
controls.evidence_requirement: Breach notification procedure; submitted breach reports.

controls.title: Data Retention and Erasure (Rule 8)
controls.description: Personal data must be erased when the specified purpose is no longer served and retention is not otherwise required by law; specified classes of fiduciaries (e.g., e-commerce, gaming, social media platforms meeting user thresholds) must erase data after a defined inactivity period, such as three years, with prior notice to the principal.
controls.test_criteria: Review the retention/erasure schedule and automated deletion/notice workflows.
controls.evidence_requirement: Retention policy; deletion logs; user notice records issued before erasure.

controls.title: Processing of Children's Data
controls.description: Data Fiduciaries must obtain verifiable parental consent before processing a child's (under 18) personal data, and are prohibited from undertaking tracking, behavioral monitoring, or targeted advertising directed at children, subject to prescribed exemptions.
controls.test_criteria: Review the age-verification and verifiable-parental-consent mechanisms.
controls.evidence_requirement: Age-gating/verification workflow; parental consent records.

controls.title: Data Principal Rights
controls.description: Data Principals have rights to access information about processing, request correction/erasure of personal data, seek grievance redressal, and nominate a representative in case of death or incapacity.
controls.test_criteria: Review the rights request handling process and response timeliness.
controls.evidence_requirement: Data principal request log; grievance redressal records.

controls.title: Grievance Redressal Mechanism
controls.description: Data Fiduciaries must publish the business contact information of a Grievance Officer and respond to grievances within a prescribed period.
controls.test_criteria: Review the published grievance contact information and grievance response-time records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Published grievance officer contact details; grievance log with response times.

controls.title: Cross-Border Data Transfer Restrictions
controls.description: Transfer of personal data outside India is permitted by default except to countries restricted by the Central Government (a blacklist/negative-list model), and sector-specific laws may impose additional localization requirements.
controls.test_criteria: Review the cross-border transfer mapping against the Government's restricted-country list.
controls.evidence_requirement: Data transfer register; legal review of destination-country status.

controls.title: Exemptions
controls.description: Certain processing is exempt or partially exempt, including state functions related to sovereignty/security, legal/judicial processing, research/statistical/archiving purposes meeting prescribed standards, and employment-related processing.
controls.test_criteria: Review exemption determinations and the supporting legal rationale.
controls.evidence_requirement: Exemption assessment memo.

controls.title: Data Protection Board Engagement
controls.description: Organizations must maintain procedures to respond to inquiries, orders, and proceedings of the Data Protection Board of India.
controls.test_criteria: Review the procedure for handling Board correspondence and any prior interactions with the Board.
controls.evidence_requirement: Regulatory correspondence log; legal response procedure.

controls.title: Records of Processing and Data Mapping
controls.description: Organizations should maintain internal records of personal data processing activities to support compliance demonstration and the technical measures required under Rule 6.
controls.test_criteria: Review the Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) for completeness and currency.
controls.evidence_requirement: RoPA document; data flow diagrams.

controls.title: Data Processor / Vendor Obligations
controls.description: Data Fiduciaries remain responsible for compliance by data processors engaged under contract; contracts must bind processors to the fiduciary's instructions and security obligations.
controls.test_criteria: Review data processing agreements with vendors for the required clauses.
controls.evidence_requirement: Vendor/processor contracts; due diligence records.

controls.title: Consent Withdrawal Mechanism
controls.description: Data Principals must be able to withdraw consent as easily as it was given, with withdrawal effective prospectively, triggering cessation of processing and instruction to processors within a reasonable time.
controls.test_criteria: Review the consent withdrawal workflow for parity with the consent-giving process and confirm processor notification.
controls.evidence_requirement: Consent withdrawal workflow; processor notification logs.

controls.title: Intimation Before Erasure for Specified Fiduciaries
controls.description: Specified classes of Data Fiduciaries, per Rule-notified thresholds, must give the Data Principal prior intimation (e.g., 48 hours) before erasing personal data due to inactivity, allowing the principal to log in or respond.
controls.test_criteria: Review pre-erasure notification logs and their timing against the Rule-prescribed window.
controls.evidence_requirement: Pre-erasure notice records.

controls.title: Independent Data Audit (Significant Data Fiduciaries)
controls.description: Significant Data Fiduciaries must undergo periodic independent data audits assessing compliance with the Act and Rules, with findings reported to the Board as required.
controls.test_criteria: Review the independent audit scope, findings, and remediation tracking.
controls.evidence_requirement: Independent audit report; remediation plan.

controls.title: Processing for State/Government Functions
controls.description: Processing of personal data by or for the State for specified functions, such as benefits, services, and licenses, is subject to modified obligations; organizations acting as intermediaries to government functions should document the applicable legal basis.
controls.test_criteria: Review the legal basis documentation for government-function processing.
controls.evidence_requirement: Legal basis memo; government notification reference.

name: DPDPA
description: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 is the primary statute governing processing of digital personal data in India, establishing principle-based obligations for Data Fiduciaries and rights for Data Principals, enforced by the Data Protection Board of India; this entry reflects the Act's own provisions independent of the 2025 Rules' implementation detail.
notes: This entry is intentionally distinct from the paired 'DPDPA 2023 (Integrated 2025 Rules)' entry: it reflects the Act, 2023 as a free-standing statutory skeleton -- principle-based duties, data principal rights, and broad delegations to future rules -- without the granular procedural detail (notice format, specific breach-notification timelines, consent manager registration mechanics, security-safeguard specifics) that the DPDP Rules, 2025 fill in. Use this entry for assessing Act-level statutory obligations and governance intent; use the paired '(Integrated 2025 Rules)' entry for operational/procedural compliance now that the Rules are in force (notified November 13, 2025).

controls.title: Lawful Grounds for Processing
controls.description: Personal data may be processed only on the basis of consent given by the Data Principal or for 'legitimate uses' enumerated in the Act, such as voluntarily provided data for a specified purpose, specified state functions, medical emergencies, and employment purposes.
controls.test_criteria: Review processing activities against the enumerated legitimate-use grounds in Sections 4 and 7, or confirm valid consent capture.
controls.evidence_requirement: Legal basis assessment per processing activity.

controls.title: Notice Requirement (Act-level)
controls.description: The Data Fiduciary must give notice to the Data Principal describing the personal data collected and the purpose of processing, provided in or accompanied by a request for consent, or as soon as reasonably practicable for legitimate-use processing predating the Act.
controls.test_criteria: Review notice content against the minimum elements required by Section 5.
controls.evidence_requirement: Privacy notice text.

controls.title: Conditions for Valid Consent
controls.description: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous, given through clear affirmative action, limited to data necessary for the specified purpose, and as easily withdrawable as it was given.
controls.test_criteria: Review the consent capture mechanism against the conditions set out in Section 6.
controls.evidence_requirement: Consent capture workflow documentation.

controls.title: General Obligations of Data Fiduciaries
controls.description: Data Fiduciaries must ensure data accuracy and completeness where used for decisions or disclosure to third parties, implement reasonable security safeguards, report breaches, and erase data when the purpose is served or consent is withdrawn, absent another legal retention basis.
controls.test_criteria: Review the Data Fiduciary's compliance program against the general obligations in Section 8.
controls.evidence_requirement: Compliance program documentation; breach reporting procedure; erasure records.

controls.title: Processing of Children's Data
controls.description: The Data Fiduciary must obtain verifiable consent from a parent or lawful guardian before processing a child's personal data, and must not undertake processing likely to cause detriment to a child, or tracking, behavioral monitoring, or targeted advertising directed at children.
controls.test_criteria: Review the verifiable-parental-consent mechanism and prohibitions on child-directed tracking/advertising.
controls.evidence_requirement: Parental consent workflow; policy prohibiting child tracking/advertising.

controls.title: Additional Obligations of Significant Data Fiduciaries
controls.description: Entities designated as Significant Data Fiduciaries by the Central Government must appoint a Data Protection Officer, appoint an independent auditor, and conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments and periodic compliance audits, with implementation mechanics left to future rules.
controls.test_criteria: Review the entity's designation status and preparedness for Significant Data Fiduciary-level obligations.
controls.evidence_requirement: SDF readiness assessment; DPO role charter.

controls.title: Right to Access Information
controls.description: Data Principals have the right to obtain a summary of personal data processed and processing activities, the identities of other fiduciaries/processors with whom data has been shared, and other prescribed information.
controls.test_criteria: Review the process for responding to access requests.
controls.evidence_requirement: Access request procedure; sample responses.

controls.title: Right to Correction and Erasure
controls.description: Data Principals have the right to correction, completion, updating, and erasure of their personal data, subject to the purpose of processing and legal retention requirements.
controls.test_criteria: Review correction/erasure request handling against defined timelines.
controls.evidence_requirement: Correction/erasure request log.

controls.title: Right to Grievance Redressal
controls.description: Data Fiduciaries must provide a readily available means for Data Principals to register grievances regarding processing or the exercise of their rights.
controls.test_criteria: Review grievance mechanism availability and response records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Grievance mechanism documentation; response log.

controls.title: Right to Nominate
controls.description: Data Principals have the right to nominate another individual to exercise their rights in the event of death or incapacity.
controls.test_criteria: Review the nomination capture mechanism offered to Data Principals.
controls.evidence_requirement: Nomination workflow/records.

controls.title: Cross-Border Transfer (Act-level)
controls.description: The Central Government may restrict transfer of personal data to specified countries or territories by notification; absent such restriction, transfer outside India is generally permitted, subject to other applicable law.
controls.test_criteria: Review transfer destinations against any government-notified restricted list in force.
controls.evidence_requirement: Transfer destination register; legal tracking of notified restrictions.

controls.title: Exemptions
controls.description: The Act exempts or modifies obligations for processing necessary for enforcement of legal rights/claims, judicial/regulatory functions, specified state functions relating to sovereignty, security, and public order, research/archiving/statistical purposes meeting prescribed standards, and processing by small or startup entities as notified.
controls.test_criteria: Review exemption claims and the supporting legal rationale.
controls.evidence_requirement: Exemption assessment memo.

controls.title: Data Protection Board Establishment and Process
controls.description: The Act establishes the Data Protection Board of India with powers to inquire into breaches, impose penalties under the Act's Schedule (up to INR 250 crore for certain failures), and issue directions; entities must be prepared to engage with Board proceedings.
controls.test_criteria: Review awareness of Board processes and the internal escalation procedure for regulatory inquiries.
controls.evidence_requirement: Regulatory engagement procedure.

controls.title: Reasonable Security Safeguards (Act-level Principle)
controls.description: Data Fiduciaries must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure compliance with the Act and to prevent personal data breach; the Act states this duty at a principle level, leaving mechanics to subsequent rules.
controls.test_criteria: Review the existence of a security program aligned to the Act's general duty, pending Rules-level specificity.
controls.evidence_requirement: Information security policy; risk assessment.

name: ISO 42001:2023
description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is the first international standard specifying requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS), applicable to organizations that provide or use AI products and services.
notes: Published December 2023; follows the Annex SL high-level structure (compatible with ISO 27001/9001) with AI-specific Annex A controls, Annex B implementation guidance, and Annex C AI-related organizational objectives and risk sources.

controls.title: Context of the Organization
controls.description: The organization must determine internal/external issues, interested parties' needs and expectations, and the scope of the AIMS relevant to its AI systems.
controls.test_criteria: Review the AIMS scope document and context analysis.
controls.evidence_requirement: AIMS scope statement; stakeholder analysis.

controls.title: Leadership and AI Policy
controls.description: Top management must demonstrate leadership, establish an AI policy, and assign AI-related roles, responsibilities, and authorities.
controls.test_criteria: Review AI policy approval and the assignment of AI governance roles.
controls.evidence_requirement: Approved AI policy; organizational roles documentation.

controls.title: Planning (Risk, Opportunity, and Objectives)
controls.description: The organization must identify AI-related risks and opportunities using Annex C risk sources, set AI objectives, and plan to achieve them through an AI risk assessment and risk treatment process.
controls.test_criteria: Review the AI risk assessment methodology, risk register, and documented objectives with plans.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI risk register; risk treatment plan; AIMS objectives documentation.

controls.title: Support (Resources, Competence, Awareness)
controls.description: The organization must provide resources, ensure competence of personnel involved in AI lifecycle activities, and maintain documented information for the AIMS.
controls.test_criteria: Review resourcing, competence records, and document control for the AIMS.
controls.evidence_requirement: Training/competence records; document control register.

controls.title: Operational Planning and Control
controls.description: The organization must plan, implement, and control processes to meet AIMS requirements, including an AI system impact assessment and lifecycle controls.
controls.test_criteria: Review operational procedures covering the AI system development and deployment lifecycle.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI lifecycle procedure documentation; impact assessment records.

controls.title: Performance Evaluation
controls.description: The organization must monitor, measure, analyze, and evaluate AIMS performance, including internal audit and management review.
controls.test_criteria: Review internal audit reports and management review minutes.
controls.evidence_requirement: Internal audit reports; management review records.

controls.title: Improvement
controls.description: The organization must address nonconformities, take corrective action, and continually improve the AIMS.
controls.test_criteria: Review nonconformity and corrective action records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Corrective action log.

controls.title: AI Policies
controls.description: The organization must establish AI policies aligned to organizational objectives, legal/regulatory requirements, and ethical principles such as fairness, transparency, and accountability.
controls.test_criteria: Review the AI policy content for coverage of required thematic areas.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI policy document.

controls.title: Internal Organization (Roles and Responsibilities)
controls.description: The organization must define roles and responsibilities for AI governance, including escalation paths for AI-related risks and incidents.
controls.test_criteria: Review the AI governance structure and RACI documentation.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI governance charter; RACI matrix.

controls.title: Resources for AI Systems
controls.description: The organization must document and manage resources needed for AI systems, including data resources, tooling/technology resources, human resources, and compute resources.
controls.test_criteria: Review the resource inventory and management procedures for AI-specific resources.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI resource inventory; compute/tooling management records.

controls.title: Assessing Impacts of AI Systems
controls.description: The organization must conduct AI system impact assessments evaluating effects on individuals and society, including fairness, safety, and security risk sources described in Annex B/C.
controls.test_criteria: Review the AI impact assessment methodology and completed assessments.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI impact assessment reports.

controls.title: AI System Lifecycle
controls.description: The organization must establish and implement processes for responsible design, development, verification/validation, deployment, operation, monitoring, and decommissioning of AI systems.
controls.test_criteria: Review AI system lifecycle procedures and gate reviews.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI system lifecycle procedure; development/validation records.

controls.title: Data for AI Systems
controls.description: The organization must manage data quality, provenance, and governance for AI training, testing, and operational data, including documentation of data sources.
controls.test_criteria: Review data governance procedures specific to AI datasets.
controls.evidence_requirement: Data lineage/provenance documentation; data quality assessment records.

controls.title: Information for Interested Parties
controls.description: The organization must determine the need for and provide information to interested parties, such as users and regulators, about AI systems, including their intended purpose and limitations.
controls.test_criteria: Review disclosure materials provided to interested parties.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI system documentation/datasheets; public disclosures.

controls.title: Use of AI Systems
controls.description: The organization must establish processes for responsible use of AI systems, including third-party-developed systems, with monitoring for intended use and misuse.
controls.test_criteria: Review the AI system use policy and monitoring for off-label use or misuse.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI acceptable use policy; usage monitoring logs.

controls.title: Third-Party and Customer Relationships
controls.description: The organization must manage AI-related risks arising from third-party suppliers, such as model and data providers, and address AI-specific requirements in customer relationships and contracts.
controls.test_criteria: Review third-party AI risk assessments and contractual AI clauses.
controls.evidence_requirement: Vendor AI risk assessments; contract clauses addressing AI obligations.

controls.title: AI-Specific Risk Source Identification
controls.description: The organization must consider AI-specific risk sources, per Annex B/C guidance, such as bias, lack of transparency, robustness and security of models, and societal impact, when performing risk assessment.
controls.test_criteria: Review risk assessment inputs for coverage of AI-specific risk categories.
controls.evidence_requirement: Risk assessment worksheets referencing Annex C risk sources.

controls.title: AI Objectives and Organizational Measurement
controls.description: The organization must set measurable AI-related objectives, such as fairness metrics and robustness targets, aligned with Annex C example objectives, and monitor progress against them.
controls.test_criteria: Review documented AI objectives and performance tracking against them.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI objectives register; KPI tracking reports.

controls.title: AI Incident Management
controls.description: The organization should establish a process to detect, report, and respond to AI system incidents or near-misses, such as harmful outputs, bias incidents, or safety failures.
controls.test_criteria: Review the AI incident response procedure and incident log.
controls.evidence_requirement: AI incident response plan; incident log.

controls.title: Human Oversight of AI Systems
controls.description: The organization must define and implement mechanisms for human oversight over AI system operation and decision-making, appropriate to the system's risk level.
controls.test_criteria: Review human oversight design and intervention capability for AI systems.
controls.evidence_requirement: Human oversight procedure; override/intervention test records.

name: NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500
description: New York's Department of Financial Services Cybersecurity Regulation (23 NYCRR Part 500) requires banks, insurers, and other DFS-regulated financial services entities operating in New York to maintain a comprehensive cybersecurity program, as amended by the Second Amendment (adopted November 2023, phased in through November 2025).
notes: Reflects the Second Amendment to Part 500 (adopted November 1, 2023) with phased compliance dates through November 1, 2025, at which point remaining obligations such as MFA under 500.12 and asset inventory under 500.13(a) became fully mandatory for covered entities. Verify exact current obligations and any newer guidance (e.g., NYDFS July 2025 MFA guidance) against the live regulation text, as secondary sources disagree on specific details such as the incident-notification window.

controls.title: Cybersecurity Program
controls.description: Covered entities must maintain a cybersecurity program based on a risk assessment, designed to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information systems.
controls.test_criteria: Review the cybersecurity program documentation against risk assessment findings.
controls.evidence_requirement: Cybersecurity program document; risk assessment report.

controls.title: Cybersecurity Policy
controls.description: Covered entities must implement a written, board or senior-officer-approved cybersecurity policy addressing the 14 areas specified in the regulation, such as access controls, data governance, incident response, and vendor management.
controls.test_criteria: Review the approved cybersecurity policy for coverage of all 14 required areas.
controls.evidence_requirement: Approved cybersecurity policy; board/senior officer approval record.

controls.title: CISO Designation and Reporting
controls.description: Covered entities must designate a qualified CISO responsible for the cybersecurity program, who must report in writing at least annually to the board (or equivalent governing body) on the program's status, material risks, and effectiveness.
controls.test_criteria: Review the CISO designation and the content/delivery of the annual report.
controls.evidence_requirement: CISO appointment record; annual CISO report to the board.

controls.title: Penetration Testing and Vulnerability Assessment
controls.description: Covered entities must conduct annual penetration testing and periodic (biannual, or continuous for Class A companies) vulnerability assessments, informed by the risk assessment.
controls.test_criteria: Review penetration test and vulnerability assessment reports and their cadence.
controls.evidence_requirement: Penetration test reports; vulnerability scan reports and remediation tracking.

controls.title: Audit Trail
controls.description: Covered entities must maintain audit trail systems designed to detect and respond to cybersecurity events and reconstruct material financial transactions, retaining records for required periods (generally 3-5 years).
controls.test_criteria: Review audit trail/logging system configuration and retention compliance.
controls.evidence_requirement: Logging system configuration; log retention policy/records.

controls.title: Access Privileges and Management
controls.description: Covered entities must limit user access privileges to systems with nonpublic information based on need, and periodically review access privileges, at least annually.
controls.test_criteria: Review the access privilege inventory and periodic access review records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Access review reports; privileged access inventory.

controls.title: Application Security
controls.description: Covered entities must have written procedures, guidelines, and standards for secure in-house application development, and procedures to evaluate the security of externally developed applications.
controls.test_criteria: Review secure SDLC documentation and third-party application security assessment records.
controls.evidence_requirement: Secure development policy; application security review/testing records.
